Philippines DOH · 90-minute course

Build your own POM

POM = Public Opinion Monitor. Taiwan CDC's system that reads television news for public-health signals. Today you build a mini version of it, then add your own idea.

Public Opinion MonitorColab + your own Claude Code

Hands-on

Today's flow

1Our POMa full tour of the real system
2Connect your Claude to Colabone message sets up the tools, then open the notebook
3Your mini POMrun it from start to end: a basic, half-finished base
4Bonus challengesteams use Claude to make it better
5Shareshow your result as a one-page HTML

Every step shows what to do and a screenshot of what you should see. Backup: if the link to Colab fails twice, use the backup track in the appendix.

Our POM, 1 of 9

POM: Public Opinion Monitor

  • Taiwan CDC's system. It watches 10 Taiwanese 24-hour news channels.
  • One frame per channel every 3 seconds. It reads the headline and the ticker separately.
  • 328 tracked public-health terms. An AI checks the hits every 10 minutes.
  • Every number opens down to the broadcast frame.

Our POM, 2 of 9

The dashboard

  1. 1Word cloud: a bigger word means more screenshots.
  2. 2Filters: today, 7 days or any date; all, public health or other.
  3. 3Keyword chips by category: tick the ones you want.
  4. 4Trend line for the keywords you tick.
  5. 5Insights ticker: what is new compared with the previous window.
  6. 6Heatmap button: the next slides.

Our POM, 3 of 9

Click a word, see the frames

  • Click any word: you get every broadcast frame behind it.
  • Frames are grouped by story and by channel.
  • Each frame shows the channel, the time and the text that was read.
  • Nothing is taken from websites. Nothing is generated.

Our POM, 4 of 9

The rhythm of a keyword

  • One grid per keyword: 7 days x 24 hours.
  • A darker cell means more frames in that hour.
  • It shows when a topic is on air, not only how much.
  • Each keyword is shaded against its own range.

Our POM, 5 of 9

Watch it read, live

  • Pick a channel and see its live frame.
  • The headline box (blue) and ticker box (green) are drawn on the picture.
  • The text read from each box appears right below.
  • A layout check runs every 12 hours. A person fixes the boxes.

Our POM, 6 of 9

Keeping noise out

  • Scrolling tickers are merged into one story.
  • Adverts are filtered: a medicine advert is not news.
  • False triggers are learned: a keyword inside another word.
  • People can always correct the AI.

Our POM, 7 of 9

From frame to dashboard: three phases

AEvery frameon the server · 7 gates
→
BAI patrolevery 10 minutes · 8 gates
→
CSafety netspeople in charge

PASS next gate   DROP leaves, nothing stored   SKIP final   WAIT retried later   REVIEW a person decides

Countedpublic health after the text check and, where needed, the picture check
Visible, not countedother topics, advertisements, entertainment
Waiting for the AIuntagged: a hatched band on the trend chart
Waiting for a personsuspect badges, repeating-advertisement candidates

Our POM, 8 of 9

Phase A: every frame

A1Frame arrivesOne frame per channel every 3 s, from 10 live channels.
A2Crop the two regionsHeadline and ticker boxes, drawn by hand for each channel.Your Step 2
A3Did the picture change?Changed by 3% or more: read it. Unchanged: skip (but read at least every 60 s).Your Step 4
A4Read the text (OCR)PaddleOCR runs on the server. No speech recognition.Your Step 3
A5Keyword gateFalse forms are cut first, then the text is matched against 328 terms.Your Step 5
A6Merge into eventsA scrolling line becomes one event. Closed after 12 s with nothing new.
A7Record the eventEvent log, plus a clean screenshot of the real broadcast frame.

Highlighted gates are the ones your mini POM rebuilds. PaddleOCR runs on the server; your notebook uses Tesseract.

Our POM, 9 of 9

Phase B: the AI patrol

B1Pick what needs a tagEvery 10 minutes, untagged items only.
B2Group into storiesRepeats on one channel, then the same news on other channels (last 24 h).
B3Free inheritanceIf the story already has a tag, copy it. No AI call.
B4Text classificationAI reads one sentence and returns one of 9 topics.
B5Is it public health?Only public health goes on to the picture check.
B6Screenshot checkAI looks at the whole frame: news or advertisement?Your bonus AI check
B7Extra questionsIs the word really on screen? Meant literally? Flags only.
B8Write backThe tag is saved for every sentence of that story. A person's tag is never overwritten.

Phase C, people in charge: C1 suspect queue · C2 repeating advertisements · C3 manual assignment (always wins). In this course we explain C2 with POM and do not rebuild it.

Connect · 1.2

Let Claude set up the rest

1.2Let Claude set up your tools

Paste the message. Approve what Claude asks. Click Yes if Windows asks. When it reports, type /exit.

Message to paste (click the text to edit it)
I am on Windows. I want Claude Code to use Colab MCP (https://github.com/googlecolab/colab-mcp).
1. Check whether git and uv are installed. Install only what is missing (winget for git, Astral's official installer for uv).
2. Find the full path of uvx.exe and use that full path: a tool installed a minute ago may not be on PATH in this window yet.
3. Add a user-scope MCP server named colab-mcp that runs: <full path of uvx.exe> git+https://github.com/googlecolab/colab-mcp
4. Run `claude mcp get colab-mcp` and tell me the status.
If a step fails, do not stop: work out why and try another way until it works. Only ask me when you need me to click or approve something myself.
When it is done, tell me in a few lines what you did and the final status.
Screenshot to add
step 1.2

Claude installs only what is missing (git about 67 MB, uv about 16 MB), adds colab-mcp and says Connected. About 190 MB in total if nothing is installed yet (about 100 MB of it is Python and libraries). A few minutes.

Connect · before 2.1

What is Google Colab?

A notebook in your browserOne web page that mixes text and code. No install: you only need Chrome and your Google account.
Cells you run one by oneClick in a code cell and press Shift+Enter. The result appears right under it. Run from the top, down.
A computer in Google's cloudThe code does not run on your laptop. Press Connect: RAM and Disk show a Google computer is yours for now.
It forgetsLeave it idle or close the tab and the computer is taken back. Files on it disappear, so save or download what you want to keep.

Why Colab today: everyone gets the same clean computer, Tesseract installs in about a minute, and nothing touches your laptop. Later your own Claude Code will add cells to this same notebook.

From POM to mini POM

Same idea, small enough to build today

POM (production)Your mini POM (today)
Input10 live news channels5 saved clips (one is Filipino)
Picturesone frame every 3 secondsone frame every 5 seconds
Readingheadline and ticker, OCR on a serverthe same two bands, Tesseract in Colab

You rebuild the idea, not the system. Then you add one feature yourself.

Your mini POM, 1 of 5

Eight steps from video to dashboard

1A news clipa video file
2Take picturesone every 5 seconds
3Cut out two bandsheadline and ticker
4Skip repeatssame strip? reuse the text
5Read the textOCR with Tesseract
6Keep health wordsa list of 180 words
7The rowsone table, shared by all
8Charts and dashboardcounts over time

Your notebook does all eight. Each step is a few lines of Python.

Your mini POM, 2 of 5

Find the two bands

  • Orange = the headline
  • Blue = the ticker, the scrolling line
  • Everything else is ignored: faces, trees, logos.

Real frame from clip_a. Every channel lays its screen out differently, so each channel needs its own boxes.

Your mini POM, 3 of 5

Read the text, skip repeats

Your mini POM, 4 of 5

Keep only health words

  • A list of 180 words: English, plus a Filipino draft that still needs DOH review.
  • Text with no word from the list is dropped.
  • What is left is one table. Every new idea you build reads these rows.
framebandtexthits
5headlineBOHOL DECLARES DENGUE OUTBREAKOutbreak; Dengue

6headlineBOHOL DECLARES DENGUE OUTBREAKOutbreak; Dengue

Run · 4

Run the notebook: two ways

4AClaude runs it

Paste this into Claude Code. Watch the cells run in your Colab tab.

Message to paste (click the text to edit it)
My Colab notebook is open in my browser. Connect to it with your Colab tools.
Run its code cells one at a time, in order, from Step 0 down to Step 6. Do not edit, add, move or delete any cell. If a cell shows an error or the connection drops, work out why (for example run the cell again, or reconnect) and keep going. Only ask me when you need me to click something in the browser.
Do not run the bonus AI cell at the end. When Step 6 is done, tell me in one line what it found.
You should see

Cells run one by one in your Colab tab; the dashboard appears after Step 6.

4BYou run it

Click in a code cell, press Shift+Enter, and go down from Step 0 to Step 6. Wait for the ▶ to stop spinning.

Step 0 installs Tesseract (20 to 60 s). Step 6 reads all five videos: about 2 minutes. Do not stop it.

The dashboard after Step 6: keywords per video, word cloud, line charts.

Either way you end with the same dashboard. Do not run the bonus AI cell at the end of the notebook: it needs a personal key.

Your mini POM, 5 of 5

What you get

Your mini POM

A solid base, not a finished product

  • WHO also matches the pronoun who.
  • Advert text with health words counts as news.
  • Fixed boxes: each channel needs its own, and frames with no band give noise.
  • Filipino word forms are missed (nagkasakit). The Filipino word list is a draft.

It works from start to end, and it has weak spots you can see in your own table.

That is your bonus: pick one weak spot and make it better with Claude.

Bonus · four teams
How the 30 minutes work
  1. 1One direction per team (A to D). Pick together, about 3 minutes.
  2. 2Take two or three small challenges. Say the goal to your own Claude in plain words, like the WHO example. Look at what it shows you before you accept it.
  3. 3Work on the rows. rows_sample.csv is safe to start from. New columns, never edit the original.
  4. 4Make one result you can show. A table, a chart or a one-page HTML (see the Share slides). One sentence: what did you find?
  5. 5Finished early? Take the next challenge in your direction, or a hard one.
